prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider never restores `token_expiry_time` when tokens are reloaded from `TokenStorage`, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired stored token as still valid. This skips the proactive refresh check and forces a full interactive re-authorization on the next request instead of a silent token refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: OAuthClientProvider never restores `token_expiry_time` when tokens are reloaded from `TokenStorage`, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired stored token as still valid. This skips the proactive refresh check and forces a full interactive re-authorization on the next request instead of a silent token refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the defect at its source in `_initialize()` with a 4-line change (`update_token_expiry()` when stored tokens carry `expires_in`) and ships a dedicated `expired_tokens` test fixture exercising the scenario. #2875's own inline comment names this exact same missing-`token_expiry_time` cause as its motivation, but instead patches around it from inside `async_auth_flow`'s 401-handling branch by adding a new pre-reauth refresh step; it leaves `is_token_valid()` itself wrong (so any other caller of that check is still affected) and the diff shown adds no corresponding test. Taking #1784 also avoids adding a second control-flow branch to the larger, already-complex `async_auth_flow` retry logic that #2875 introduces.

prs.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
prs.author: adityuhkapoor
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json's original guard (`field_info.annotation is not str`) makes it attempt json.loads() on any parameter whose annotation is a union containing str (e.g. str | None), so a plain string value that happens to be valid JSON syntax (e.g. a numeric string, "null", or a JSON-looking payload) gets silently corrupted into a non-string type before it ever reaches Pydantic validation. prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS after a server disconnect, the code just logs and returns without ever resolving the pending request tied to that stream — the caller's request hangs forever instead of failing. Both PRs fix this same underlying 'silent give-up on reconnection failure' bug in _handle_reconnection, just via different mechanisms. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE reconnection exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS after a server disconnect, the code just logs and returns without ever resolving the pending request tied to that stream — the caller's request hangs forever instead of failing. Both PRs fix this same underlying 'silent give-up on reconnection failure' bug in _handle_reconnection, just via different mechanisms. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395 resolves the failure at the source: it checks ctx.session_message.message against JSONRPCRequest and sends a properly-correlated JSONRPCError (matching the original request id) straight to ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the affected in-flight request fails while the rest of the session stays healthy; it also upgrades the log line from debug to warning for visibility. #3098 instead raises StreamableHTTPError and adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to dig it back out of anyio ExceptionGroups — a more invasive path that risks tearing down the whole task group/connection rather than failing just the one pending request, and adds unwrap-tree traversal complexity to work around that. #2395's fix is scoped to the actual failure point and doesn't require the exception-group unwrapping workaround.

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address the same root cause: stdio_server creates its internal read/write memory object streams with buffer size 0, which means a handler trying to send a message (e.g. a final response) blocks until stdout_writer has fully drained a prior write (e.g. an in-flight progress notification). #2215 exposes this as a caller-configurable parameter (read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size, both still defaulting to 0), so the deadlock/blocking scenario is unchanged unless a caller opts in and knows to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1. #2654 instead fixes the default itself by hardcoding the write_stream buffer to 1, so the fix applies out of the box with no API change required, and it ships a concrete regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces a handler queuing its response while stdout is still flushing an earlier progress notification. (2 PRs)

prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same block in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) that mishandles an assistant message containing tool_use when the following message has no tool_result blocks — currently it wrongly raises 'ids of tool_result blocks and tool_use blocks from previous message do not match' since tool_result_ids ends up as the empty set. members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both address the same root cause: stdio_server creates its internal read/write memory object streams with buffer size 0, which means a handler trying to send a message (e.g. a final response) blocks until stdout_writer has fully drained a prior write (e.g. an in-flight progress notification). #2215 exposes this as a caller-configurable parameter (read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size, both still defaulting to 0), so the deadlock/blocking scenario is unchanged unless a caller opts in and knows to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1. #2654 instead fixes the default itself by hardcoding the write_stream buffer to 1, so the fix applies out of the box with no API change required, and it ships a concrete regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces a handler queuing its response while stdout is still flushing an earlier progress notification.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both address the same root cause: stdio_server creates its internal read/write memory object streams with buffer size 0, which means a handler trying to send a message (e.g. a final response) blocks until stdout_writer has fully drained a prior write (e.g. an in-flight progress notification). #2215 exposes this as a caller-configurable parameter (read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size, both still defaulting to 0), so the deadlock/blocking scenario is unchanged unless a caller opts in and knows to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1. #2654 instead fixes the default itself by hardcoding the write_stream buffer to 1, so the fix applies out of the box with no API change required, and it ships a concrete regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces a handler queuing its response while stdout is still flushing an earlier progress notification.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 resolves the failure at the source: it checks ctx.session_message.message against JSONRPCRequest and sends a properly-correlated JSONRPCError (matching the original request id) straight to ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the affected in-flight request fails while the rest of the session stays healthy; it also upgrades the log line from debug to warning for visibility. #3098 instead raises StreamableHTTPError and adds a recursive _unwrap_exception helper to dig it back out of anyio ExceptionGroups — a more invasive path that risks tearing down the whole task group/connection rather than failing just the one pending request, and adds unwrap-tree traversal complexity to work around that. #2395's fix is scoped to the actual failure point and doesn't require the exception-group unwrapping workaround.

clusters.pick_reason: #2492 requires extending the `TokenStorage` protocol with new `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods; because these default to no-ops, every existing `TokenStorage` implementation must be updated to actually implement them before the fix takes effect, and persisted metadata is trusted on reload with no re-validation. #3263 fixes cold-start refresh for all existing `TokenStorage` implementations without changing that interface at all — it performs discovery before the cold-start refresh call, adds an `eager_discovery_attempted` flag on `OAuthContext` so a metadata-less server isn't re-probed on every in-process refresh, and additionally adds an issuer-binding check on the discovered metadata that #2492's persisted-metadata path doesn't perform.

members.author: Bartok9
